title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building the Teichmüller tower and groupoid explicitly from pants decompositions. A type G is a trivalent 'graph with open edges': vertices S, half-edges (flags) \vec{\hat A}, an involution σ whose fixed points I are the open edges (marked points), and edges A. Â = A ⊔ I.

(1) Model of one pair of pants. The previous page fixes a model for P^1 with three marked points. It is the round unit sphere Σ_I with a great circle E_R (the real locus, or equator). The three points I sit on E_R as an inscribed equilateral triangle, which makes the configuration invariant under G_3 = S_3. Around each i ∈ I one takes the geodesic circle Γ_{i,ρ} of fixed radius ρ, small enough that the three circles are disjoint. Each Γ_{i,ρ} meets the equator in two diametrically opposite points. Sending each of these to the nearest of the two other marked points gives a canonical bijection Γ_{i,ρ} ∩ E_R ≅ I∖{i}.

(2) The circle as a torsor. Since the two points are antipodal on the oriented metric circle Γ_{i,ρ}, one gets a canonical isomorphism of U-torsors Γ_{i,ρ} ≅ U ∧^{{±1}} (I∖{i}). Here U is the unit circle group. In words, the circle is the U-torsor obtained from the {±1}-torsor I∖{i} by extension of structure group along {±1} ⊂ U. This uses both the orientation and the arc-length.

(3) Gluing the stable curve. The maximally degenerate curve X_G of type G is obtained from its normalisation ⊔_{s∈S} Σ_{\vec{\hat A}_s} (one standard sphere per vertex, marked by its three flags) by identifying points according to σ.
- For each x ∈ Â, a U-torsor T_x is defined.
- For x ∈ I (a marked point at vertex s): T_x ≅ U ∧^{±1} (\vec{\hat A}_s ∖ x). This is the circle of real tangent directions at the marked point, with its two 'real' directions.
- For x ∈ A (a node with flags x̃, σx̃): T_x ≅ U ∧^{±1} ∧_{x̃ over x} (\vec{\hat A}_{σ(x̃)} ∖ {x̃}). This is the contracted product of the two two-element sets, i.e. the circle of arguments of gluing (plumbing) parameters in T_p ⊗ T_q, the twist-angle torsor.
- NB: if x is a loop (both flags at one vertex s, third flag y), then σ induces a canonical identification of the two two-element sets {σx̃, y} and {x̃, y}. The product torsor is therefore trivial and T_x ≅ U canonically.

(4) What this serves (next page). P_G = ∏_x T_x is a U^{Â}-torsor; together with radii in ]0,1[^A it maps to moduli. Hence one gets π_1 = Z^{Â} (Dehn twists, including boundary twists) → the Teichmüller group. The finite set Sε_G = ∏ ε_a of 2^{card A} 'real' points (the real gluings, twist 0 or π at each node) provides canonical base points. The subgroupoid S_0 T_G on these base points maps to the Teichmüller groupoid. This is a concrete, real-structure-based construction of tangential base points at infinity attached to each pants decomposition.
errors: Notational slip: X̃_G = ⊔_{s∈G} should be ⊔_{s∈S} (vertices), as in the next line. Γ_{ij} in the transcription is Γ_{i,ρ}. 'E_0' and 'E_R' denote the same equator. No mathematical error detected.
Implicit hypothesis: the U-torsor identification of Γ_{i,ρ} needs the orientation and the normalised arc-length parametrisation of the circle; this is assumed from the previous page.

ideas.what: Circle around a marked point, with two antipodal real points, identified canonically with U ∧^{±1} of a two-element set (extension of structure group {±1} → U)
ideas.modern_name: Real tangential directions / unit tangent circle as a torsor induced from the real structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara–Nakamura for the Teichmüller setting
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only alludes to base points 'at infinity'

ideas.what: Twist torsor at a node as the contracted product of the torsors of the two branches; canonically trivial for a loop
ideas.modern_name: Plumbing/gluing parameter in T_p⊗T_q; Fenchel–Nielsen twist angle torsor

ideas.what: Maximally degenerate curve of type G built from standard equilateral spheres glued by σ, with 2^{card A} real gluings as canonical base points for the Teichmüller groupoid
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points at maximally degenerate (real) stable curves; vertices of the Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps / Bakalov–Kirillov Teichmüller (Lego) groupoid
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2–3 describes the Teichmüller tower and pants-decomposition base points only qualitatively

missed.claim: An explicit, metric-canonical (G_3-invariant equilateral-sphere) construction of the 2^{card A} real tangential base points per pants decomposition, including the canonical trivialisation for loop edges. It predates the published Teichmüller-groupoid constructions by about two decades. The ideas are now known, but this specific early formulation (torsor bookkeeping via U ∧^{±1}) is undocumented.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the base-point choices underlying the Teichmüller (Lego) groupoid and the GT action. The ±-choices per edge (real gluings) foreshadow the half-twist/orientation data in Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps and Bakalov–Kirillov.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, explicit early version of the base-point construction for the Teichmüller groupoid. The mathematics itself is now standard (Deligne, Ihara–Nakamura, HLS), so it is mainly of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: 'Γ_{ij}' should read Γ_{i,ρ} (circle of radius ρ centred at i).
'X̃_G = ⊔_{s∈G} Σ_{Â_s}': the image has Σ_{\vec{\hat A}_s}; the index should be s∈S.
Struck-out text in the parenthesis is '(Z × {±1})' over '{±1}', i.e. the intended map is {±1} → U.
